producer_report.summary: Added the design note docs/design/continuous-landing.md for throughput review 20261105-070420-vq95. After the verifier passes, the job joins the one ordered landing queue and its pull request merges automatically through the existing REST path (`land_pr`, `merge_via_rest`). A job whose poll ends pending stays in the queue, with a time limit H at the head, then a second limit before it goes to the user. A refused merge goes to the user at once. The rebuild keeps its lock, because a landing moves the checkout the build reads, and runs once per batch with bounds K landings or M minutes. The note labels 420.0 min as the review's prediction. It names the measurement: the median over the newest 20 landings (`THROUGHPUT_WINDOW`, `StageMinutes::median_of`), from the verifier's end to the landing record, against 464.5 and 440.1. It also asks the next review to report rebuild time separately. It also has an Existing code table (reused or changed per row), alternatives, risks, out of scope, five ordered build jobs (the first splits the 440.1 min by phase) and the citation duty. Besides the note, I added two pointer sentences to async-drain.md (no renumbering), decision D155 in decisions.md and one Unreleased CHANGELOG entry. I ran the policy, backtest, ontology, budgets, refusal_corpus and lifecycle tests, and all pass. I also ran the full `cargo test --locked` once, but its output was too large to read, so I have no pass or fail result from that run.

open_issues: Acceptance criterion 8 says only docs/design/ changes, but the expected deliverables also list docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md. I edited both, since neither is a governance file. Drop them if the user wants only docs/design/.
Host question: is GitHub's native auto-merge enabled on the repository? The code does not show it. The design does not depend on it.
The split of the 440.1 minutes by phase is unmeasured. The limits H, K and M, and the size of the saving, depend on build job 1.
The full `cargo test --locked` result was not seen by me; Athena's recorded test check is the authority for it.
mistakes: I ran the full `cargo test --locked` before checking that its output could be read. It was too large and sat outside the working directory, so I could not confirm the result and had to fall back to targeted runs.
learnings: THROUGHPUT.md is not in the working copy or the evidence snapshot; the figures come only from the request text.

hestia.md says no record separates the rebuild from the landing stage. In drain.rs a job's own rebuild runs after its landing in `finish`, but the code read does not show whether the outcome record is written before or after the rebuild. The note leaves that to build job 1.

Landing::Waiting is produced when the poll ends with the pull request open and checks pending, including a merge refused under repository rules (landing_from_report); `land_pr` keeps reading checks inside the same poll budget.
`cargo test` output from a long run is persisted outside the working directory, and the Read and Grep tools refuse that path, so large outputs cannot be inspected.
desires: A way to read the tail of a large command output inside the working directory, to confirm a full-suite result.
